caption: The drawing depicts a single object, which is an elongated oval or teardrop-shaped cap with a pointed end at the bottom, labeled as a beaded cap from the Ojibway Tribe. The cap is highly decorated with intricate patterns. The central part of the cap contains a floral motif with layered shapes colored in blues, pinks, yellows, and blacks, outlined in what appears to be black or dark gray. Surrounding the center is a series of concentric decorative borders: an inner border with small, closely spaced magenta or purple dots, an outer white border, and a wider outermost border with alternating black and white elements. At the pointed end at the bottom, there is a knotted cloth or ribbon depicted using soft grayish shading, indicating folds and texture. The background of the drawing is plain, light beige paper. On the left side of the paper, handwritten text reads “Ojibway Tribe CAP (BEADED) EASTERN Woodland Hall CASE 8 W.” On the right, text reads “Dec. 2nd 1935” and a signature, “Mary Benson.” The top edge of the paper has a row of perforations, indicating it was removed from a notebook.
title: Cap
